subject: telescope
reasoning:
I'm designing a refractor telescope on a tripod with an alt-az mount, roughly 1.4m tall, with a root joint and additional joints for altitude and azimuth rigging so the parts can articulate properly.

Working out the tripod legs, spreader tray, and mount pillar, then building the tube assembly angled upward at about 35 degrees with a dew shield, lens cell, objective glass disc, and a focuser with eyepiece at the back end.

I'm defining a helper to position parts along the tube's direction and perpendicular offset, setting up the torus rings around the tube oriented with its axis, and establishing a joint hierarchy with root, azimuth, and altitude bones tying tripod, mount, and tube parts together.

Now I'm computing the three tripod leg feet positions around the head at equal angles, splitting each leg into an upper wooden rod and a thinner lower metal rod joined by a clamp collar, and adding a rubber tip sphere at the foot — making sure the lower rod ends flush at ground level with flat caps rather than round ones so nothing sinks below the floor.

For the spreader, I'm placing a three-sided cylinder at the height where the legs cross, checking that its circumradius matches the leg spread at that point, and adding a center knob on top. Then I'm setting up the mounting pillar above the spreader with a bolt and head cylinder for the camera mount.

Now I'm building the fork assembly: two arm boxes extending upward from the mount head, an altitude axis running horizontally between them with brass knobs capping the ends, and tube pivot clamps wrapping around the telescope tube at that axis point. I'm checking the tube's rear end position to make sure the eyepiece doesn't collide with the mount head below, and confirming the geometry clears properly.

Picking a color palette now: cream-white tube, navy accents, brass, black, wood tripod, metal gray. Adding a glass lens disc with slight purple tint, and planning a hollow dew shield using a lathe profile.

Also sketching the finder scope: a small black rod with a bell front, held by two bracket rings connected to the main tube by small rods.

Now turning to the focuser assembly at the rear—end cap, focuser body, draw tube, and eyepiece barrel with a rubber flare, stacked along the tube axis with decreasing radii, plus a pair of focus knobs positioned along the x-axis.

I'm also setting up a bone assignment system and writing helper functions—a point-placement function using position, direction, and offset vectors, and a cylinder helper that handles radius, span, offset, color, and bone attachment for building the lengthwise tube segments.

For the torus component, I'm specifying z-axis orientation, then working through tripod leg rods with tapered radii using a dedicated rod function, and placing small foot spheres at the ends to cap them off flush with the ground.

Now I'm adding leg lock collars oriented along each leg direction, a head plate cylinder near the top, and a thin center rod running from the head down to the accessory tray. Then I'm setting up the joint hierarchy starting with the root at the origin.
